All seven threads replied to and resolved; CI is running on the new commit. Summary of the round:

## All seven comments were correct. Two were real bugs.

**The serious one:** `computeMultiRangeDeletionVerdict` pushed each range's roots as a *single* `deleteSubtreeGroups` group. Once a range's cover is a mixed-depth forest, those roots span parents, `resolveContiguousGroup` rejects, and the user's whole multi-range deletion is **vetoed** — refused outright, not degraded. Both deletion paths now share `groupRootsByParent`.

I should be straight about why this shipped: my task 3.4 asserted that path "needs no shape change," and the test I wrote to back it passed **one** edit — which `computeVerdictForRanges` delegates straight to `computeVerdict`, never entering the multi-range branch. A vacuous test guarding a false claim, which is the exact failure mode I'd written up in Q30 one commit earlier. The reviewer caught it because the test was visibly not exercising what it named.

**Performance:** two Θ(n²) loops. `ForestRoot` now carries the `path` and per-root `cover` the walk already computes, so grouping needs no `findPath` per root and chrome needs no `nodeStartLine` + `subtreeCoverOf` per root. I'd added `startLineIndex` specifically to keep the geometry linear, then had both consumers throw it away.

**Docs:** the proposal still claimed `src/ops.ts` gains normalization, `src/classify.ts`'s gate widens, and the multi-range path needs no change. All three were disproved during implementation; I'd corrected `design.md` and `tasks.md` but not the proposal.

## One thing worth flagging about my own process

Chasing the copy/paste test, I reported a paste regression that **did not exist**. I'd been suppressing `npm run build:plugin` output and running `npx wdio` directly — which, unlike `npm run test:e2e`, does not build. Combined with a `git stash` and a worktree, several probes ran against a `main.js` that didn't match the source. I measured carefully and drew confident conclusions from the wrong artifact, twice, before checking that the binary was current. On a verified build, mixed-depth copy→paste behaves correctly and matches `main`.

Net: 1890 unit, 17/17 desktop, 17/17 mobile, lint and both typechecks clean, vault drift clean.

The two `test-vault/` files you were editing are still untouched and unstaged — I excluded them from the commit.

test: close the two coverage gaps the second review round found

Both were tests that passed for the wrong reason.

The deletion property asserted `encode(parse(applied)) === applied` — a
round-trip, not an orphan check. `finalize` already emits a parsed/encoded
document, so it held for a no-op deletion, and it held when a parent was
removed and its indented descendants simply re-parsed as new roots, which
is the exact orphan it claimed to rule out. It now compares against an
independently constructed expectation: an escalated cover's roots tile a
contiguous span and each carries its own trailing gap, so the deletion
must remove exactly the lines in [lo, hi] and leave every other line
byte-identical — computable from the span without reference to how the
deletion was implemented. Verified by negative control (delete one root
per group instead of all, watch it fail).

Per-root chrome had no automated coverage at all. Every scenario in
63-selection-visual-treatment is single-rooted, and single-rooted covers
anchor identically under both the new and the old implementation — so the
one-target-for-the-whole-range version passed every test in the suite,
including the four this PR added elsewhere. The new case uses HEADINGS
deliberately: a list item's own additive shift is 0 because list guides
defer to Obsidian's native rendering, so a pure-list mixed-depth cover
would anchor identically either way and prove nothing. Asserts the two
roots do not share a column and that a descendant follows its own root.
Verified by negative control.

Also corrected: design D4's consumer table still said the classification
gate widens, contradicting the measured conclusion fifteen lines below;
and the org-mode divergence row overstated the invariant as "a selection
is always a forest of whole subtrees" when within-node selections pass
through as ordinary character selections.
EOF
git push 2>&1 | tail -2

content.text:
Second review round addressed and pushed. No inline threads this time — all four were *suppressed* comments, so there was nothing to reply to individually; I posted a summary comment on the PR instead.

**All four were valid, and two were the same failure mode as the first round: tests passing for the wrong reason.**

The sharper one is the chrome coverage. The reviewer's actual point wasn't "add a test" — it was that **the old one-target implementation still passed every test I'd added**. That's true, and it means my per-root chrome change was resting entirely on a screenshot I looked at once. Now it has a test, verified by negative control.

Worth noting how easily that test could also have been vacuous: the obvious fixture is a nested list, and a list item's own additive shift is `0` because list guides defer to Obsidian's native rendering — so a pure-list mixed-depth cover anchors identically under both implementations. It would have passed, proved nothing, and looked like coverage. It uses headings for exactly that reason. I only knew because I'd measured it earlier when judging 7.2.

The deletion property had the same shape: `encode(parse(applied)) === applied` is a round-trip, and since `finalize` already emits a parsed/encoded document it held for a no-op deletion *and* for the orphan case it was named after. It now compares against an independently derived expectation.

Both doc fixes were mine to have caught — D4's table row still said the gate widens, fifteen lines above the text explaining that it doesn't.

Verification: unit 1890, desktop 17/17, mobile 17/17, lint and typechecks clean. CI running; I'll report when it lands.

Three things remain open, unchanged and all yours: the `waitForNotice` flake decision, tasks 7.1/7.3, and the stale-`main.js` guard I suggested. I haven't acted on any of them.
